ring2_rationale.win: Engine output up and the castings constraint addressed: superalloy/titanium (ATI, Carpenter) and CFM partner Safran.
ring2_rationale.lose: GE taking engine deliveries and aftermarket share from Pratt & Whitney (RTX).

ring2_rationale.win: More solid-rocket-motor capacity unblocks missile primes (Lockheed, RTX).
ring2_rationale.lose: Budget and missile mix shifting to munitions primes over Boeing's defence programmes — weak.

ring2_rationale.win: Aerojet motor growth unblocks Lockheed and RTX missile deliveries.
ring2_rationale.lose: Munitions primes gain budget share relative to Boeing defence — weak.

ring2_rationale.win: CFM deliveries and aftermarket strength pull engine materials (ATI, Carpenter) and castings (Howmet).
ring2_rationale.lose: Narrowbody CFM strength contrasts with Rolls-Royce's widebody-only exposure — weak.

ring2_rationale.win: Missiles segment up with backlog: motors (L3Harris, Northrop) and magnets (MP).
ring2_rationale.lose: Lockheed winning missile/fighter budget share relative to Boeing defence.

ring2_rationale.win: Raytheon air-defence backlog up: motors (Northrop), magnets (MP), and castings for Pratt (Howmet).
ring2_rationale.lose: Missile/air-defence budget share over Boeing defence — weak.

ring2_rationale.win: ATI citing aero/defence demand confirms engine build rates at GE Aerospace and Howmet.
ring2_rationale.lose: Titanium/nickel tightness raises input cost for airframers (Boeing) — weak.

ring2_rationale.win: 155mm ramp and combat-systems growth: read-through to munitions peers (Rheinmetall) and energetics/motors (Northrop).
ring2_rationale.lose: Budget shifting to munitions over Boeing defence platforms — weak.

ring2_rationale.win: Howmet engine-products growth pulls superalloy/titanium (ATI, Carpenter) and reflects CFM build (Safran).

ring2_rationale.lose: US submarine programme on track keeps AUKUS work in US yards rather than BAE's — weak.

ring2_rationale.win: NdPr above 1,000t secures magnet supply for missile primes (Lockheed, RTX).

ring2_rationale.lose: European procurement preferring European primes over US imports (Lockheed) — weak.

ring2_rationale.win: 100k rounds/month confirms the munitions cycle; read-through to European ammunition makers (Rheinmetall, BAE).
ring2_rationale.lose: Budget shifting to munitions over Boeing defence platforms — weak.
